key_insight: The paper introduces an online memory mechanism for dynamic novel view synthesis that keeps long-range scene information without requiring expensive gradient updates at every frame. In simple terms, it aims to make real-time view synthesis both memory-aware and computationally efficient.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of reconstructing dynamic scenes from streaming multi-view video under strict real-time constraints. Existing test-time training methods can remember occluded content, but their frame-by-frame gradient updates are too slow for practical online use.
method: Uses an online neural space-time memory to store and retrieve scene information across frames.
Replaces heavy per-frame gradient-based memory updates with a more efficient update strategy suited for streaming inputs.
Targets dynamic motion and temporary occlusions by preserving long-horizon context while keeping inference fast.
impact: This matters because it makes memory-based novel view synthesis more practical for real-world streaming applications such as robotics, AR/VR, and live 3D capture. For practitioners, the key value is better temporal consistency and occlusion handling without sacrificing real-time performance.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing streaming multi-view input → neural memory → novel view output.

paper_title: Online Neural Space Time Memory for Dynamic Novel View Synthesis
paper_authors: Baback Elmieh, Lynn Tsai, Zeman Li, Srinivas Kaza, Tiancheng Sun
